intro: Calibration residuals can turn point predictions into intervals. The finite-sample rank uses n+1, so small calibration sets need special care at high coverage.
task: Construct a calibrated interval radius from the corrected finite-sample rank, rejecting a requested rank that cannot produce a finite threshold.
requirements: residuals is a nonempty vector of nonnegative absolute calibration errors; predictions is a finite vector, possibly empty; 0<alpha<1.
Use rank k=ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)), counting from one. Reject when k>n because this finite-valued contract cannot represent the required infinite threshold.
Let q be the kth smallest residual. Return dict radius as q, lower as predictions-q, and upper as predictions+q. Exchangeability is an interpretation assumption, not a validation check.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Keep ranks one-based until indexing
hints.body: Compute the corrected rank before subtracting one for array indexing.

hints.title: Do not silently clip an impossible rank
hints.body: A requested finite threshold may not exist for the calibration-set size.

explanation: Split conformal uses heldout residuals to choose an error threshold. The corrected rank is more conservative than an ordinary sample percentile and matters most for small samples.
Coverage interpretation requires exchangeability between calibration and future examples. The code constructs intervals but does not assert that the assumption holds in a deployed system.
